## Plot the dots - SPC charts

```{r}
library(NHSRdatasets)
library(NHSRplotthedots)

data <- NHSRdatasets::ae_attendances

data_spc <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code == 'RVR', type == '1')

data_spc |>
  NHSRplotthedots::ptd_spc(value_field = attendances, 
                           date_field = period)
```


## Over to you

- Add in a target of 17,500
- Show improvement as a reduction

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(
  minutes = 7,
  color_border = "#005EB8",
  color_text = "#005EB8",
  color_running_text = "white",
  color_running_background = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_text = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_background = "white",
  margin = "0.9em",
  font_size = "2em"
)
```

## Answer - adding target and improvement to SPC

```{r}
data_spc |>
  NHSRplotthedots::ptd_spc(
    value_field = attendances,
    date_field = period,
    target = 17500,
    improvement_direction = 'decrease'
  )
```

## Facetting an SPC

We now want to create a chart for each attendance type

```{r}
data_spc <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code == 'RVR')

data_spc |>
  NHSRplotthedots::ptd_spc(
    value_field = attendances,
    date_field = period,
    improvement_direction = 'decrease',
    facet_field = type
  )
```


## Improving the chart

Not bad but looks a bit clumpy and we need to tweak a few things to make this 
a pretty `ggplot`

First turn our ptd_spc into an object:

```{r}
plot_spc <- data_spc |>
  NHSRplotthedots::ptd_spc(
    value_field = attendances,
    date_field = period,
    improvement_direction = 'decrease',
    facet_field = type
  )

```

## Feed that object into ptd_create_ggplot

```{r}
plot_spc |>
  NHSRplotthedots::ptd_create_ggplot(
    fixed_y_axis_multiple = FALSE,
    x_axis_date_format = "%b %y",
    x_axis_breaks = "2 months"
  )

```


## Over to you - prepare data

- Create a faceted plot for type 1 attendances RQM, RJ1 and RDD

:::{.callout-tip collapse=false appearance='default' icon=true}
This will require creating a data object followed by an SPC plot object
:::


```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(
  minutes = 5,
  color_border = "#005EB8",
  color_text = "#005EB8",
  color_running_text = "white",
  color_running_background = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_text = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_background = "white",
  margin = "0.9em",
  font_size = "2em"
)
```

## Answer - create dataset

```{r}
data_spc <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RDD'), 
         type == '1')

plot_spc <- data_spc |>
  NHSRplotthedots::ptd_spc(
    value_field = attendances,
    date_field = period,
    improvement_direction = 'decrease',
    facet_field = org_code
  )

```

## Over to you - improve the plot SPC

- Change the point size to look nicer
- Change the x axis label to date rather than period
- Make any other changes you feel would be useful to describe chart

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(
  minutes = 7,
  color_border = "#005EB8",
  color_text = "#005EB8",
  color_running_text = "white",
  color_running_background = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_text = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_background = "white",
  margin = "0.9em",
  font_size = "2em"
)
```

## Answer - alter the SPC plot

```{r}
plot_spc |>
  NHSRplotthedots::ptd_create_ggplot(
    fixed_y_axis_multiple = FALSE,
    x_axis_date_format = "%b %y",
    x_axis_breaks = "2 months",
    point_size = 2,
    main_title = 'Prettier SPC plot',
    x_axis_label = 'Date',
    icons_position = "top left",
    icons_size = 12
  )
```
